g1.label: 1. Overall, car use ___ over the period
g1.why: Car journeys went from 52% to 35% — an overall fall.

g2.label: 2. The share of bus journeys ___
g2.why: Bus use went up and down between 28% and 31%. “Fluctuate” is from the IELTS Vocabulary Glossary.

g3.label: 3. then dropped ___ to 41%
g3.why: A fall of 8 points in two years is the biggest drop on the graph — sharply.

g4.label: 4. car use continued to ___
g4.why: It kept getting smaller, 41% → 35%. “Dwindle” is from the IELTS Vocabulary Glossary.

g5.label: 5. cycling ___ at around 13% until 2018
g5.why: It hardly changed (12% → 13% → 13%), so it remained stable.

g6.label: 6. It then increased ___ to 22%
g6.why: From 13% to 22% in two years is a very large jump — dramatically.

g7.label: 7. Bus journeys ___ between 28% and 31%
g7.why: Moving up and down within a narrow range is fluctuating.

g8.label: 8. the gap had ___ from 40 to 8 points
g8.why: A gap that gets smaller (40 → 8 points) narrows.

g1.label: 1. There was a ___ in car use
g1.why: After “there was a” you need a noun phrase: adjective + noun.

g2.label: 2. Car use ___ after 2018
g2.why: The sentence needs a verb, and an adverb (sharply) describes a verb.

g3.label: 3. Cycling saw a ___
g3.why: “Saw a …” needs a noun, so use adjective + noun.

g4.label: 4. bus journeys ___ over the decade
g4.why: Verb + adverb: the adverb “slightly” describes how it fluctuated.

g5.label: 5. The figures show a ___
g5.why: After “show a” you need a noun phrase: adjective + noun.

g6.label: 6. Sales ___ in the final year
g6.why: Verb + adverb: “gradually” describes how sales rose.

g7.label: 7. Prices ___ between 2019 and 2021
g7.why: “Remain” is like “be”: it is followed by an adjective (stable), not an adverb.

g8.label: 8. 2020 saw a ___ in cycling
g8.why: “Saw a …” needs a noun phrase: adjective + noun.

g1.label: 1. fell ___ 52% to 35%
g1.why: “From … to …” gives the starting and finishing figures.

g2.label: 2. dropped ___ 41%
g2.why: 41% is the new figure it reached, so use “to”.

g3.label: 3. rose ___ 15 percentage points
g3.why: 15 points is the size of the change (12% → 27%), so use “by”.

g4.label: 4. peaked ___ 31%
g4.why: A highest point is “at” a figure: peaked at 31%.

g5.label: 5. a rise ___ 9 percentage points
g5.why: After the noun “rise”, the size of the change takes “of”.

g6.label: 6. car use stood ___ 52%
g6.why: “Stand at” gives the level at one point in time.

g7.label: 7. cycling climbed ___ 22%
g7.why: 22% is the figure it reached, so use “to”.

g8.label: 8. a fall ___ 3 percentage points
g8.why: After the noun “fall”, the size of the change takes “of” (52% → 49%).
